summary: Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around the sulphuric-acid chokepoint with a two-lane map: one obvious copper reference name that proves the node is economically relevant, and three underfollowed second-order candidates tied to chemical distribution, bulk-liquid logistics, and acid-processing technology. The most direct underfollowed US-listed candidate found in this pass is Hawkins, because it explicitly receives, stores, distributes and sells sulfuric acid in bulk. Kirby and KBR are adjacent chokepoint hypotheses: Kirby may matter if rerouted acid and agricultural/industrial chemicals tighten US bulk-liquid barge capacity, while KBR may matter if acid recovery, purification, reconcentration, or critical-minerals processing capex accelerates. None of these are recommendations; each requires later revenue-materiality and customer-flow verification.
